<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[en:Kannazuki]][[it:Kannazuki]][[ja:神無月]][[ko:신무월]][[uk:Каннадзукі]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q6364021]] Wikidata name: Kannazuki [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:18, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:22, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:02, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Lunisolar October|qq=}} {{for|the Japanese comedian|Kannazuki (comedian)|qq=}} {{Italic title|qq=}} {{refimprove|date=November 2020|qq=}} {{nihongo|'''''Kannazuki'''''|神無月||also ''Kaminazuki'', ''Kaminashizuki''|qq=}} is a traditional name for the tenth month in the traditional [[Japanese calendar]]. Sometimes called Lunar [[:en:October|October]].
The name can be translated literally as "the month when there are no gods".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Izumo|title=Izumo {{!|qq=}} Japan|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> In [[Shinto]] tradition it was said that the eight million gods of Japan left their shrines and congregated annually at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]]. There the month was known as {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神在月|qq=}}, "the month when the gods are present".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kamiarizuki|title=Kamiarizuki {{!|qq=}} Shinto|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> However, the 無 character, which normally means "absent" or "there is not", is here probably originally used as an [[:en:Ateji|Ateji]], that is used only for the sound "na". In this name the "na" is actually a possessive particle, so ''Kaminazuki'' means "month of the gods", not "month without gods" ''(Kaminakizuki)'', similarly to ''Minazuki'', the "month of water". However, by false etymology this became commonly interpreted to mean that because in that month, all the Shinto ''[[kami]]'' gather at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Shrine]] in Izumo province (modern-day [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]]), there are no gods in the rest of the country with the exception of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], who does not hear the summons and is thus still available for worship. Thus, in Izumo Province, the month is called {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神有月 or 神在月|"month with gods"|qq=}}.
Until 1873, the tenth month of the lunar calendar largely overlapped with the modern month of November. However, after the adoption of the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]] in Japan in that year, October became generally accepted as the "godless month".
==October (Lunisolar)==
'''Lunisolar October''' (旧暦10月) is the tenth [[:en:Month|Month (calendar)]] of the {{ill|Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} ([[:en:Lunisolar calendar|Lunisolar calendar]]).
Before the adoption of the [[:en:Tenpō calendar|Tenpō calendar]], Lunisolar October was defined as the month containing [[:en:Xiaoxue|Shōsetsu (solar term)]]. In the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|New Calendar]], it corresponds roughly to late [[:en:October|October]] through early [[:en:December|December]].
Lunisolar October is also called {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|神無月|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, although in {{ill|Izumo Province|ja|Izumo Province|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, particularly in [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], it is referred to as {{ill|Kamiarizuki|ja|神在月|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiarizuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} or {{ill|Kamiaritsuki|ja|神有月|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiaritsuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}}. For the etymology, see [[#Etymology]]{{efn|October|ja|10月|qq=draft}}.
In the East Asian lunisolar calendar, the number of days in each month ({{ill|Days in a lunar month|ja|大小|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Days in a lunar month|1=Large and Small|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10935019}}, 30-day "big months" and 29-day "small months") varies by year. As a result, some years have only 29 days in Lunisolar October, making {{ill|October 30 (Lunisolar)|ja|10月30日 (旧暦)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 30 (Lunisolar)|qq=}} nonexistent.
==Overview==
'''Kannazuki''' (神無月, also read as ''Kaminazuki''<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>), alternatively written as ''Kamnazuki''<ref name="ReferenceA">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.412, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>, ''Kaminashizuki,'' or ''Kaminakarizuki''<ref name="ReferenceB">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 978-4167598082</ref>, is an name for the {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|10月 (旧暦)|lt=10th month of the Japanese Lunar Calendar|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. In modern times, it is also commonly used as an alternate name for October in the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]. The interpretation of "神無" ("absence of gods") is a {{ill|folk etymology|ja|語源俗解|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/folk etymology|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 民間語源|1=folk etymology|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109964}}, which later gave rise to various legends (discussed below).
== Etymology == {{See also|October|qq=}} The origin of the term "Kannazuki" is unclear. A prominent theory suggests that the "na" in "Kannazuki" is a possessive particle meaning "of," thus translating to "Month of the Gods." This interpretation is supported by the [[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]]. This is analogous to the term [[:en:Minazuki|Minazuki]] ("Month of Water"), where "na" also functions as a possessive particle (see {{ill|June#Etymology of Minazuki|ja|6月#水無月の語源|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June#Etymology of Minazuki|1=June|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q120}}).
The belief that all [[:en:Kami|kami (Shinto deities)]] gather at {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} for an annual meeting, leaving other regions devoid of deities, is a later interpretation from the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]. This folk etymology was spread nationwide by the {{ill|Onshi|ja|御師|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onshi|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} of [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]].<ref>Such folk explanations appear in texts like "Ōgishō" (旺文社古語辞典, 8th ed., p.332, 1994).</ref><ref>The attribution of "神無月" to the 10th month likely began in the Heian period. Theories on its meaning include "Month of Brewing" (醸成月) and "Month of Kannamesai" (神嘗月) (Suzuki Tōzō, 日常語語源辞典, p.80, Tōkyōdō, 1992).</ref><ref>Takashima Toshio noted, "Kannazuki has ancient folk etymologies, suggesting it means 'month without gods,' which arose from misunderstanding the original meaning of 'Kaminazuki'" (高島俊男, お言葉ですが, p.88, Bungeishunjū, 2006).</ref>
Even in [[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa Prefecture]], where Onshi activities were absent, the lunar October is called "飽果十月" (meaning "fruitless October") because no religious events are held during this time.<ref name='gyoji'>{{Cite book |editor=[[Nishikado Masayoshi]] |date=1958-05-23 |title=Encyclopedia of Annual Events |publisher=Tōkyōdō Shuppan |page=18|qq=}}</ref>

Consequently, in Izumo, October is called '''Kamiarizuki''' (神在月 or 神有月, meaning "Month with Gods"), reflecting the opposite belief. This folk belief has been present since the [[:en:Middle Ages|medieval period]].<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.120, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976.</ref>

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[en:Kannazuki]][[it:Kannazuki]][[ja:神無月]][[ko:신무월]][[uk:Каннадзукі]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q6364021]] Wikidata name: Kannazuki [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:18, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:22, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:02, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Lunisolar October|qq=}} {{for|the Japanese comedian|Kannazuki (comedian)|qq=}} {{Italic title|qq=}} {{refimprove|date=November 2020|qq=}} {{nihongo|'''''Kannazuki'''''|神無月||also ''Kaminazuki'', ''Kaminashizuki''|qq=}} is a traditional name for the tenth month in the traditional [[Japanese calendar]]. Sometimes called Lunar [[:en:October|October]].
The name can be translated literally as "the month when there are no gods".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Izumo|title=Izumo {{!|qq=}} Japan|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> In [[Shinto]] tradition it was said that the eight million gods of Japan left their shrines and congregated annually at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]]. There the month was known as {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神在月|qq=}}, "the month when the gods are present".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kamiarizuki|title=Kamiarizuki {{!|qq=}} Shinto|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> However, the 無 character, which normally means "absent" or "there is not", is here probably originally used as an [[:en:Ateji|Ateji]], that is used only for the sound "na". In this name the "na" is actually a possessive particle, so ''Kaminazuki'' means "month of the gods", not "month without gods" ''(Kaminakizuki)'', similarly to ''Minazuki'', the "month of water". However, by false etymology this became commonly interpreted to mean that because in that month, all the Shinto ''[[kami]]'' gather at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Shrine]] in Izumo province (modern-day [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]]), there are no gods in the rest of the country with the exception of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], who does not hear the summons and is thus still available for worship. Thus, in Izumo Province, the month is called {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神有月 or 神在月|"month with gods"|qq=}}.
Until 1873, the tenth month of the lunar calendar largely overlapped with the modern month of November. However, after the adoption of the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]] in Japan in that year, October became generally accepted as the "godless month".
==October (Lunisolar)==
'''Lunisolar October''' (旧暦10月) is the tenth [[:en:Month|Month (calendar)]] of the {{ill|Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} ([[:en:Lunisolar calendar|Lunisolar calendar]]).
Before the adoption of the [[:en:Tenpō calendar|Tenpō calendar]], Lunisolar October was defined as the month containing [[:en:Xiaoxue|Shōsetsu (solar term)]]. In the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|New Calendar]], it corresponds roughly to late [[:en:October|October]] through early [[:en:December|December]].
Lunisolar October is also called {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|神無月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, although in {{ill|Izumo Province|ja|Izumo Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, particularly in [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], it is referred to as {{ill|Kamiarizuki|ja|神在月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiarizuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} or {{ill|Kamiaritsuki|ja|神有月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiaritsuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}}. For the etymology, see [[#Etymology]]{{efn|October|ja|10月|qq=draft}}.
In the East Asian lunisolar calendar, the number of days in each month ({{ill|Days in a lunar month|ja|大小|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Days in a lunar month|1=Large and Small|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10935019}}, 30-day "big months" and 29-day "small months") varies by year. As a result, some years have only 29 days in Lunisolar October, making {{ill|October 30 (Lunisolar)|ja|10月30日 (旧暦)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 30 (Lunisolar)|qq=}} nonexistent.
==Overview==
'''Kannazuki''' (神無月, also read as ''Kaminazuki''<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>), alternatively written as ''Kamnazuki''<ref name="ReferenceA">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.412, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>, ''Kaminashizuki,'' or ''Kaminakarizuki''<ref name="ReferenceB">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 978-4167598082</ref>, is an name for the {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|10月 (旧暦)|lt=10th month of the Japanese Lunar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. In modern times, it is also commonly used as an alternate name for October in the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]. The interpretation of "神無" ("absence of gods") is a {{ill|folk etymology|ja|語源俗解|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/folk etymology|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 民間語源|1=folk etymology|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109964}}, which later gave rise to various legends (discussed below).
== Etymology == {{See also|October|qq=}} The origin of the term "Kannazuki" is unclear. A prominent theory suggests that the "na" in "Kannazuki" is a possessive particle meaning "of," thus translating to "Month of the Gods." This interpretation is supported by the [[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]]. This is analogous to the term [[:en:Minazuki|Minazuki]] ("Month of Water"), where "na" also functions as a possessive particle (see {{ill|June#Etymology of Minazuki|ja|6月#水無月の語源|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June#Etymology of Minazuki|1=June|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q120}}).
The belief that all [[:en:Kami|kami (Shinto deities)]] gather at {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} for an annual meeting, leaving other regions devoid of deities, is a later interpretation from the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]. This folk etymology was spread nationwide by the {{ill|Onshi|ja|御師|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onshi|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} of [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]].<ref>Such folk explanations appear in texts like "Ōgishō" (旺文社古語辞典, 8th ed., p.332, 1994).</ref><ref>The attribution of "神無月" to the 10th month likely began in the Heian period. Theories on its meaning include "Month of Brewing" (醸成月) and "Month of Kannamesai" (神嘗月) (Suzuki Tōzō, 日常語語源辞典, p.80, Tōkyōdō, 1992).</ref><ref>Takashima Toshio noted, "Kannazuki has ancient folk etymologies, suggesting it means 'month without gods,' which arose from misunderstanding the original meaning of 'Kaminazuki'" (高島俊男, お言葉ですが, p.88, Bungeishunjū, 2006).</ref>
Even in [[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa Prefecture]], where Onshi activities were absent, the lunar October is called "飽果十月" (meaning "fruitless October") because no religious events are held during this time.<ref name='gyoji'>{{Cite book |editor=[[Nishikado Masayoshi]] |date=1958-05-23 |title=Encyclopedia of Annual Events |publisher=Tōkyōdō Shuppan |page=18|qq=}}</ref>
== Folk Traditions Based on "Kami Absent" == The idea that deities gather in {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} during October led to the belief that this region experiences a divine presence while the rest of Japan does not. Consequently, in Izumo, October is called '''Kamiarizuki''' (神在月 or 神有月, meaning "Month with Gods"), reflecting the opposite belief. This folk belief has been present since the [[:en:Middle Ages|medieval period]].<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.120, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976.</ref>
=== Kami Arrival and Departure Rituals === ==== In Izumo ==== In Izumo, several shrines, including [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], conduct rituals known as "Kamiarizuki" during the lunar October: * On the night of {{ill|10th day of the 10th lunar month|ja|10月10日 (旧暦)|1=October 10 (Lunisolar)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10th day of the 10th lunar month|13=User:Immanuelle/October 10 (Lunisolar)|qq=}}, the {{ill|Kami-mukae-sai|ja|神迎祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-mukae-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Welcoming of the Deities") is held at {{ill|Inasa Beach|ja|稲佐浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inasa Beach|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲佐の浜}}. This is followed by the {{ill|Kamiari-sai|ja|神在祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiari-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} at Izumo Taisha from the 11th to the 17th, with the {{ill|Karasade-sai|ja|神等去出祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karasade-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Farewell of the Deities") on the 18th.
==== In Nagano ==== At {{ill|Mount Iizuna|ja|飯綱山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Iizuna|1=Mount Iizuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666650}} in Nagano, rituals for "sending off" and "welcoming back" deities from Izumo were traditionally held. These events, involving torch-lighting, were discontinued after fires occurred in the Meiji period.<ref>{{Cite book |author=Nagano Prefecture Saku City Board of Education |date=1978-11-15 |title=Oral Legends of Kita-Saku |page=78|qq=}}</ref>

==October (Lunisolar)==
'''Lunisolar October''' (旧暦10月) is the tenth [[:en:Month|Month (calendar)]] of the {{ill|Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} ([[:en:Lunisolar calendar|Lunisolar calendar]]).
Before the adoption of the [[:en:Tenpō calendar|Tenpō calendar]], Lunisolar October was defined as the month containing [[:en:Xiaoxue|Shōsetsu (solar term)]]. In the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|New Calendar]], it corresponds roughly to late [[:en:October|October]] through early [[:en:December|December]].
Lunisolar October is also called {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|神無月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, although in {{ill|Izumo Province|ja|Izumo Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, particularly in [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], it is referred to as {{ill|Kamiarizuki|ja|神在月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiarizuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} or {{ill|Kamiaritsuki|ja|神有月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiaritsuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}}. For the etymology, see [[#Etymology]]{{efn|October|ja|10月|qq=draft}}.
In the East Asian lunisolar calendar, the number of days in each month ({{ill|Days in a lunar month|ja|大小|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Days in a lunar month|1=Large and Small|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10935019}}, 30-day "big months" and 29-day "small months") varies by year. As a result, some years have only 29 days in Lunisolar October, making {{ill|October 30 (Lunisolar)|ja|10月30日 (旧暦)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 30 (Lunisolar)|qq=}} nonexistent.
==Overview==
'''Kannazuki''' (神無月, also read as ''Kaminazuki''<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>), alternatively written as ''Kamnazuki''<ref name="ReferenceA">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.412, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>, ''Kaminashizuki,'' or ''Kaminakarizuki''<ref name="ReferenceB">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 978-4167598082</ref>, is an name for the {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|10月 (旧暦)|lt=10th month of the Japanese Lunar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. In modern times, it is also commonly used as an alternate name for October in the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]. The interpretation of "神無" ("absence of gods") is a {{ill|folk etymology|ja|語源俗解|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/folk etymology|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 民間語源|1=folk etymology|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109964}}, which later gave rise to various legends (discussed below).
== Etymology == {{See also|October|qq=}} The origin of the term "Kannazuki" is unclear. A prominent theory suggests that the "na" in "Kannazuki" is a possessive particle meaning "of," thus translating to "Month of the Gods." This interpretation is supported by the [[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]]. This is analogous to the term [[:en:Minazuki|Minazuki]] ("Month of Water"), where "na" also functions as a possessive particle (see {{ill|June#Etymology of Minazuki|ja|6月#水無月の語源|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June#Etymology of Minazuki|1=June|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q120}}).
The belief that all [[:en:Kami|kami (Shinto deities)]] gather at {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} for an annual meeting, leaving other regions devoid of deities, is a later interpretation from the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]. This folk etymology was spread nationwide by the {{ill|Onshi|ja|御師|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onshi|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} of [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]].<ref>Such folk explanations appear in texts like "Ōgishō" (旺文社古語辞典, 8th ed., p.332, 1994).</ref><ref>The attribution of "神無月" to the 10th month likely began in the Heian period. Theories on its meaning include "Month of Brewing" (醸成月) and "Month of Kannamesai" (神嘗月) (Suzuki Tōzō, 日常語語源辞典, p.80, Tōkyōdō, 1992).</ref><ref>Takashima Toshio noted, "Kannazuki has ancient folk etymologies, suggesting it means 'month without gods,' which arose from misunderstanding the original meaning of 'Kaminazuki'" (高島俊男, お言葉ですが, p.88, Bungeishunjū, 2006).</ref>
Even in [[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa Prefecture]], where Onshi activities were absent, the lunar October is called "飽果十月" (meaning "fruitless October") because no religious events are held during this time.<ref name='gyoji'>{{Cite book |editor=[[Nishikado Masayoshi]] |date=1958-05-23 |title=Encyclopedia of Annual Events |publisher=Tōkyōdō Shuppan |page=18|qq=}}</ref>
== Folk Traditions Based on "Kami Absent" == The idea that deities gather in {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} during October led to the belief that this region experiences a divine presence while the rest of Japan does not. Consequently, in Izumo, October is called '''Kamiarizuki''' (神在月 or 神有月, meaning "Month with Gods"), reflecting the opposite belief. This folk belief has been present since the [[:en:Middle Ages|medieval period]].<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.120, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976.</ref>
=== Kami Arrival and Departure Rituals === ==== In Izumo ==== In Izumo, several shrines, including [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], conduct rituals known as "Kamiarizuki" during the lunar October: * On the night of {{ill|10th day of the 10th lunar month|ja|10月10日 (旧暦)|1=October 10 (Lunisolar)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10th day of the 10th lunar month|13=User:Immanuelle/October 10 (Lunisolar)|qq=}}, the {{ill|Kami-mukae-sai|ja|神迎祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-mukae-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Welcoming of the Deities") is held at {{ill|Inasa Beach|ja|稲佐浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inasa Beach|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲佐の浜}}. This is followed by the {{ill|Kamiari-sai|ja|神在祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiari-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} at Izumo Taisha from the 11th to the 17th, with the {{ill|Karasade-sai|ja|神等去出祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karasade-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Farewell of the Deities") on the 18th.
==== In Nagano ==== At {{ill|Mount Iizuna|ja|飯綱山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Iizuna|1=Mount Iizuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666650}} in Nagano, rituals for "sending off" and "welcoming back" deities from Izumo were traditionally held. These events, involving torch-lighting, were discontinued after fires occurred in the Meiji period.<ref>{{Cite book |author=Nagano Prefecture Saku City Board of Education |date=1978-11-15 |title=Oral Legends of Kita-Saku |page=78|qq=}}</ref>

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[en:Kannazuki]][[it:Kannazuki]][[ja:神無月]][[ko:신무월]][[uk:Каннадзукі]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q6364021]] Wikidata name: Kannazuki [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:18, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:22, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:02, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Lunisolar October|qq=}} {{for|the Japanese comedian|Kannazuki (comedian)|qq=}} {{Italic title|qq=}} {{refimprove|date=November 2020|qq=}} {{nihongo|'''''Kannazuki'''''|神無月||also ''Kaminazuki'', ''Kaminashizuki''|qq=}} is a traditional name for the tenth month in the traditional [[Japanese calendar]]. Sometimes called Lunar [[:en:October|October]].
The name can be translated literally as "the month when there are no gods".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Izumo|title=Izumo {{!|qq=}} Japan|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> In [[Shinto]] tradition it was said that the eight million gods of Japan left their shrines and congregated annually at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]]. There the month was known as {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神在月|qq=}}, "the month when the gods are present".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kamiarizuki|title=Kamiarizuki {{!|qq=}} Shinto|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> However, the 無 character, which normally means "absent" or "there is not", is here probably originally used as an [[:en:Ateji|Ateji]], that is used only for the sound "na". In this name the "na" is actually a possessive particle, so ''Kaminazuki'' means "month of the gods", not "month without gods" ''(Kaminakizuki)'', similarly to ''Minazuki'', the "month of water". However, by false etymology this became commonly interpreted to mean that because in that month, all the Shinto ''[[kami]]'' gather at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Shrine]] in Izumo province (modern-day [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]]), there are no gods in the rest of the country with the exception of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], who does not hear the summons and is thus still available for worship. Thus, in Izumo Province, the month is called {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神有月 or 神在月|"month with gods"|qq=}}.
Until 1873, the tenth month of the lunar calendar largely overlapped with the modern month of November. However, after the adoption of the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]] in Japan in that year, October became generally accepted as the "godless month".
==October (Lunisolar)==
'''Lunisolar October''' (旧暦10月) is the tenth [[:en:Month|Month (calendar)]] of the {{ill|Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} ([[:en:Lunisolar calendar|Lunisolar calendar]]).
Before the adoption of the [[:en:Tenpō calendar|Tenpō calendar]], Lunisolar October was defined as the month containing [[:en:Xiaoxue|Shōsetsu (solar term)]]. In the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|New Calendar]], it corresponds roughly to late [[:en:October|October]] through early [[:en:December|December]].
Lunisolar October is also called {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|神無月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, although in {{ill|Izumo Province|ja|Izumo Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, particularly in [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], it is referred to as {{ill|Kamiarizuki|ja|神在月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiarizuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} or {{ill|Kamiaritsuki|ja|神有月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiaritsuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}}. For the etymology, see [[#Etymology]]{{efn|October|ja|10月|qq=draft}}.
In the East Asian lunisolar calendar, the number of days in each month ({{ill|Days in a lunar month|ja|大小|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Days in a lunar month|1=Large and Small|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10935019}}, 30-day "big months" and 29-day "small months") varies by year. As a result, some years have only 29 days in Lunisolar October, making {{ill|October 30 (Lunisolar)|ja|10月30日 (旧暦)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 30 (Lunisolar)|qq=}} nonexistent.

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[en:Kannazuki]][[it:Kannazuki]][[ja:神無月]][[ko:신무월]][[uk:Каннадзукі]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q6364021]] Wikidata name: Kannazuki [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:18, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:22, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:02, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Lunisolar October|qq=}} {{for|the Japanese comedian|Kannazuki (comedian)|qq=}} {{Italic title|qq=}} {{refimprove|date=November 2020|qq=}} {{nihongo|'''''Kannazuki'''''|神無月||also ''Kaminazuki'', ''Kaminashizuki''|qq=}} is a traditional name for the tenth month in the traditional [[Japanese calendar]]. Sometimes called Lunar [[:en:October|October]].
The name can be translated literally as "the month when there are no gods".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Izumo|title=Izumo {{!|qq=}} Japan|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> In [[Shinto]] tradition it was said that the eight million gods of Japan left their shrines and congregated annually at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]]. There the month was known as {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神在月|qq=}}, "the month when the gods are present".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kamiarizuki|title=Kamiarizuki {{!|qq=}} Shinto|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> However, the 無 character, which normally means "absent" or "there is not", is here probably originally used as an [[:en:Ateji|Ateji]], that is used only for the sound "na". In this name the "na" is actually a possessive particle, so ''Kaminazuki'' means "month of the gods", not "month without gods" ''(Kaminakizuki)'', similarly to ''Minazuki'', the "month of water". However, by false etymology this became commonly interpreted to mean that because in that month, all the Shinto ''[[kami]]'' gather at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Shrine]] in Izumo province (modern-day [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]]), there are no gods in the rest of the country with the exception of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], who does not hear the summons and is thus still available for worship. Thus, in Izumo Province, the month is called {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神有月 or 神在月|"month with gods"|qq=}}.
Until 1873, the tenth month of the lunar calendar largely overlapped with the modern month of November. However, after the adoption of the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]] in Japan in that year, October became generally accepted as the "godless month".
==October (Lunisolar)==
'''Lunisolar October''' (旧暦10月) is the tenth [[:en:Month|Month (calendar)]] of the {{ill|Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} ([[:en:Lunisolar calendar|Lunisolar calendar]]).
Before the adoption of the [[:en:Tenpō calendar|Tenpō calendar]], Lunisolar October was defined as the month containing [[:en:Xiaoxue|Shōsetsu (solar term)]]. In the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|New Calendar]], it corresponds roughly to late [[:en:October|October]] through early [[:en:December|December]].
Lunisolar October is also called {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|神無月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, although in {{ill|Izumo Province|ja|Izumo Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, particularly in [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], it is referred to as {{ill|Kamiarizuki|ja|神在月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiarizuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} or {{ill|Kamiaritsuki|ja|神有月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiaritsuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}}. For the etymology, see [[#Etymology]]{{efn|October|ja|10月|qq=draft}}.
In the East Asian lunisolar calendar, the number of days in each month ({{ill|Days in a lunar month|ja|大小|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Days in a lunar month|1=Large and Small|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10935019}}, 30-day "big months" and 29-day "small months") varies by year. As a result, some years have only 29 days in Lunisolar October, making {{ill|October 30 (Lunisolar)|ja|10月30日 (旧暦)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 30 (Lunisolar)|qq=}} nonexistent.
==Overview==
'''Kannazuki''' (神無月, also read as ''Kaminazuki''<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>), alternatively written as ''Kamnazuki''<ref name="ReferenceA">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.412, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>, ''Kaminashizuki,'' or ''Kaminakarizuki''<ref name="ReferenceB">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 978-4167598082</ref>, is an name for the {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|10月 (旧暦)|lt=10th month of the Japanese Lunar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. In modern times, it is also commonly used as an alternate name for October in the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]. The interpretation of "神無" ("absence of gods") is a {{ill|folk etymology|ja|語源俗解|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/folk etymology|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 民間語源|1=folk etymology|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109964}}, which later gave rise to various legends (discussed below).
== Etymology == {{See also|October|qq=}} The origin of the term "Kannazuki" is unclear. A prominent theory suggests that the "na" in "Kannazuki" is a possessive particle meaning "of," thus translating to "Month of the Gods." This interpretation is supported by the [[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]]. This is analogous to the term [[:en:Minazuki|Minazuki]] ("Month of Water"), where "na" also functions as a possessive particle (see {{ill|June#Etymology of Minazuki|ja|6月#水無月の語源|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June#Etymology of Minazuki|1=June|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q120}}).
The belief that all [[:en:Kami|kami (Shinto deities)]] gather at {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} for an annual meeting, leaving other regions devoid of deities, is a later interpretation from the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]. This folk etymology was spread nationwide by the {{ill|Onshi|ja|御師|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onshi|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} of [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]].<ref>Such folk explanations appear in texts like "Ōgishō" (旺文社古語辞典, 8th ed., p.332, 1994).</ref><ref>The attribution of "神無月" to the 10th month likely began in the Heian period. Theories on its meaning include "Month of Brewing" (醸成月) and "Month of Kannamesai" (神嘗月) (Suzuki Tōzō, 日常語語源辞典, p.80, Tōkyōdō, 1992).</ref><ref>Takashima Toshio noted, "Kannazuki has ancient folk etymologies, suggesting it means 'month without gods,' which arose from misunderstanding the original meaning of 'Kaminazuki'" (高島俊男, お言葉ですが, p.88, Bungeishunjū, 2006).</ref>
Even in [[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa Prefecture]], where Onshi activities were absent, the lunar October is called "飽果十月" (meaning "fruitless October") because no religious events are held during this time.<ref name='gyoji'>{{Cite book |editor=[[Nishikado Masayoshi]] |date=1958-05-23 |title=Encyclopedia of Annual Events |publisher=Tōkyōdō Shuppan |page=18|qq=}}</ref>
== Folk Traditions Based on "Kami Absent" == The idea that deities gather in {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} during October led to the belief that this region experiences a divine presence while the rest of Japan does not. Consequently, in Izumo, October is called '''Kamiarizuki''' (神在月 or 神有月, meaning "Month with Gods"), reflecting the opposite belief. This folk belief has been present since the [[:en:Middle Ages|medieval period]].<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.120, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976.</ref>
=== Kami Arrival and Departure Rituals === ==== In Izumo ==== In Izumo, several shrines, including [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], conduct rituals known as "Kamiarizuki" during the lunar October: * On the night of {{ill|10th day of the 10th lunar month|ja|10月10日 (旧暦)|1=October 10 (Lunisolar)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10th day of the 10th lunar month|13=User:Immanuelle/October 10 (Lunisolar)|qq=}}, the {{ill|Kami-mukae-sai|ja|神迎祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-mukae-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Welcoming of the Deities") is held at {{ill|Inasa Beach|ja|稲佐浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inasa Beach|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲佐の浜}}. This is followed by the {{ill|Kamiari-sai|ja|神在祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiari-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} at Izumo Taisha from the 11th to the 17th, with the {{ill|Karasade-sai|ja|神等去出祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karasade-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Farewell of the Deities") on the 18th.
==== In Nagano ==== At {{ill|Mount Iizuna|ja|飯綱山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Iizuna|1=Mount Iizuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666650}} in Nagano, rituals for "sending off" and "welcoming back" deities from Izumo were traditionally held. These events, involving torch-lighting, were discontinued after fires occurred in the Meiji period.<ref>{{Cite book |author=Nagano Prefecture Saku City Board of Education |date=1978-11-15 |title=Oral Legends of Kita-Saku |page=78|qq=}}</ref>

The name can be translated literally as "the month when there are no gods".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Izumo|title=Izumo {{!|qq=}} Japan|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> In [[Shinto]] tradition it was said that the eight million gods of Japan left their shrines and congregated annually at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]]. There the month was known as {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神在月|qq=}}, "the month when the gods are present".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kamiarizuki|title=Kamiarizuki {{!|qq=}} Shinto|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> However, the 無 character, which normally means "absent" or "there is not", is here probably originally used as an [[:en:Ateji|Ateji]], that is used only for the sound "na". In this name the "na" is actually a possessive particle, so ''Kaminazuki'' means "month of the gods", not "month without gods" ''(Kaminakizuki)'', similarly to ''Minazuki'', the "month of water". However, by false etymology this became commonly interpreted to mean that because in that month, all the Shinto ''[[kami]]'' gather at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Shrine]] in Izumo province (modern-day [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]]), there are no gods in the rest of the country with the exception of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], who does not hear the summons and is thus still available for worship. Thus, in Izumo Province, the month is called {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神有月 or 神在月|"month with gods"|qq=}}.
Until 1873, the tenth month of the lunar calendar largely overlapped with the modern month of November. However, after the adoption of the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]] in Japan in that year, October became generally accepted as the "godless month".
==October (Lunisolar)==
'''Lunisolar October''' (旧暦10月) is the tenth [[:en:Month|Month (calendar)]] of the {{ill|Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} ([[:en:Lunisolar calendar|Lunisolar calendar]]).
Before the adoption of the [[:en:Tenpō calendar|Tenpō calendar]], Lunisolar October was defined as the month containing [[:en:Xiaoxue|Shōsetsu (solar term)]]. In the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|New Calendar]], it corresponds roughly to late [[:en:October|October]] through early [[:en:December|December]].
Lunisolar October is also called {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|神無月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, although in {{ill|Izumo Province|ja|Izumo Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, particularly in [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], it is referred to as {{ill|Kamiarizuki|ja|神在月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiarizuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} or {{ill|Kamiaritsuki|ja|神有月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiaritsuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}}. For the etymology, see [[#Etymology]]{{efn|October|ja|10月|qq=draft}}.
In the East Asian lunisolar calendar, the number of days in each month ({{ill|Days in a lunar month|ja|大小|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Days in a lunar month|1=Large and Small|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10935019}}, 30-day "big months" and 29-day "small months") varies by year. As a result, some years have only 29 days in Lunisolar October, making {{ill|October 30 (Lunisolar)|ja|10月30日 (旧暦)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 30 (Lunisolar)|qq=}} nonexistent.
==Overview==
'''Kannazuki''' (神無月, also read as ''Kaminazuki''<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>), alternatively written as ''Kamnazuki''<ref name="ReferenceA">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.412, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>, ''Kaminashizuki,'' or ''Kaminakarizuki''<ref name="ReferenceB">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 978-4167598082</ref>, is an name for the {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|10月 (旧暦)|lt=10th month of the Japanese Lunar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. In modern times, it is also commonly used as an alternate name for October in the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]. The interpretation of "神無" ("absence of gods") is a {{ill|folk etymology|ja|語源俗解|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/folk etymology|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 民間語源|1=folk etymology|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109964}}, which later gave rise to various legends (discussed below).
== Etymology == {{See also|October|qq=}} The origin of the term "Kannazuki" is unclear. A prominent theory suggests that the "na" in "Kannazuki" is a possessive particle meaning "of," thus translating to "Month of the Gods." This interpretation is supported by the [[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]]. This is analogous to the term [[:en:Minazuki|Minazuki]] ("Month of Water"), where "na" also functions as a possessive particle (see {{ill|June#Etymology of Minazuki|ja|6月#水無月の語源|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June#Etymology of Minazuki|1=June|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q120}}).
The belief that all [[:en:Kami|kami (Shinto deities)]] gather at {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} for an annual meeting, leaving other regions devoid of deities, is a later interpretation from the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]. This folk etymology was spread nationwide by the {{ill|Onshi|ja|御師|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onshi|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} of [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]].<ref>Such folk explanations appear in texts like "Ōgishō" (旺文社古語辞典, 8th ed., p.332, 1994).</ref><ref>The attribution of "神無月" to the 10th month likely began in the Heian period. Theories on its meaning include "Month of Brewing" (醸成月) and "Month of Kannamesai" (神嘗月) (Suzuki Tōzō, 日常語語源辞典, p.80, Tōkyōdō, 1992).</ref><ref>Takashima Toshio noted, "Kannazuki has ancient folk etymologies, suggesting it means 'month without gods,' which arose from misunderstanding the original meaning of 'Kaminazuki'" (高島俊男, お言葉ですが, p.88, Bungeishunjū, 2006).</ref>
Even in [[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa Prefecture]], where Onshi activities were absent, the lunar October is called "飽果十月" (meaning "fruitless October") because no religious events are held during this time.<ref name='gyoji'>{{Cite book |editor=[[Nishikado Masayoshi]] |date=1958-05-23 |title=Encyclopedia of Annual Events |publisher=Tōkyōdō Shuppan |page=18|qq=}}</ref>
== Folk Traditions Based on "Kami Absent" == The idea that deities gather in {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} during October led to the belief that this region experiences a divine presence while the rest of Japan does not. Consequently, in Izumo, October is called '''Kamiarizuki''' (神在月 or 神有月, meaning "Month with Gods"), reflecting the opposite belief. This folk belief has been present since the [[:en:Middle Ages|medieval period]].<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.120, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976.</ref>
=== Kami Arrival and Departure Rituals === ==== In Izumo ==== In Izumo, several shrines, including [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], conduct rituals known as "Kamiarizuki" during the lunar October: * On the night of {{ill|10th day of the 10th lunar month|ja|10月10日 (旧暦)|1=October 10 (Lunisolar)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10th day of the 10th lunar month|13=User:Immanuelle/October 10 (Lunisolar)|qq=}}, the {{ill|Kami-mukae-sai|ja|神迎祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-mukae-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Welcoming of the Deities") is held at {{ill|Inasa Beach|ja|稲佐浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inasa Beach|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲佐の浜}}. This is followed by the {{ill|Kamiari-sai|ja|神在祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiari-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} at Izumo Taisha from the 11th to the 17th, with the {{ill|Karasade-sai|ja|神等去出祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karasade-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Farewell of the Deities") on the 18th.
==== In Nagano ==== At {{ill|Mount Iizuna|ja|飯綱山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Iizuna|1=Mount Iizuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666650}} in Nagano, rituals for "sending off" and "welcoming back" deities from Izumo were traditionally held. These events, involving torch-lighting, were discontinued after fires occurred in the Meiji period.<ref>{{Cite book |author=Nagano Prefecture Saku City Board of Education |date=1978-11-15 |title=Oral Legends of Kita-Saku |page=78|qq=}}</ref>

Consequently, in Izumo, October is called '''Kamiarizuki''' (神在月 or 神有月, meaning "Month with Gods"), reflecting the opposite belief. === Kami Arrival and Departure Rituals === ==== In Izumo ==== In Izumo, several shrines, including [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], conduct rituals known as "Kamiarizuki" during the lunar October: * On the night of {{ill|10th day of the 10th lunar month|ja|10月10日 (旧暦)|1=October 10 (Lunisolar)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10th day of the 10th lunar month|13=User:Immanuelle/October 10 (Lunisolar)|qq=}}, the {{ill|Kami-mukae-sai|ja|神迎祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-mukae-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Welcoming of the Deities") is held at {{ill|Inasa Beach|ja|稲佐浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inasa Beach|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲佐の浜}}. This is followed by the {{ill|Kamiari-sai|ja|神在祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiari-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} at Izumo Taisha from the 11th to the 17th, with the {{ill|Karasade-sai|ja|神等去出祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karasade-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Farewell of the Deities") on the 18th.
==== In Nagano ==== At {{ill|Mount Iizuna|ja|飯綱山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Iizuna|1=Mount Iizuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666650}} in Nagano, rituals for "sending off" and "welcoming back" deities from Izumo were traditionally held. These events, involving torch-lighting, were discontinued after fires occurred in the Meiji period.<ref>{{Cite book |author=Nagano Prefecture Saku City Board of Education |date=1978-11-15 |title=Oral Legends of Kita-Saku |page=78|qq=}}</ref>

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[en:Kannazuki]][[it:Kannazuki]][[ja:神無月]][[ko:신무월]][[uk:Каннадзукі]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q6364021]] Wikidata name: Kannazuki [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:18, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:22, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:02, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Lunisolar October|qq=}} {{for|the Japanese comedian|Kannazuki (comedian)|qq=}} {{Italic title|qq=}} {{refimprove|date=November 2020|qq=}} {{nihongo|'''''Kannazuki'''''|神無月||also ''Kaminazuki'', ''Kaminashizuki''|qq=}} is a traditional name for the tenth month in the traditional [[Japanese calendar]]. Sometimes called Lunar [[:en:October|October]].
The name can be translated literally as "the month when there are no gods".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Izumo|title=Izumo {{!|qq=}} Japan|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> In [[Shinto]] tradition it was said that the eight million gods of Japan left their shrines and congregated annually at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]]. There the month was known as {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神在月|qq=}}, "the month when the gods are present".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kamiarizuki|title=Kamiarizuki {{!|qq=}} Shinto|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> However, the 無 character, which normally means "absent" or "there is not", is here probably originally used as an [[:en:Ateji|Ateji]], that is used only for the sound "na". In this name the "na" is actually a possessive particle, so ''Kaminazuki'' means "month of the gods", not "month without gods" ''(Kaminakizuki)'', similarly to ''Minazuki'', the "month of water". However, by false etymology this became commonly interpreted to mean that because in that month, all the Shinto ''[[kami]]'' gather at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Shrine]] in Izumo province (modern-day [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]]), there are no gods in the rest of the country with the exception of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], who does not hear the summons and is thus still available for worship. Thus, in Izumo Province, the month is called {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神有月 or 神在月|"month with gods"|qq=}}.
Until 1873, the tenth month of the lunar calendar largely overlapped with the modern month of November. However, after the adoption of the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]] in Japan in that year, October became generally accepted as the "godless month".
==October (Lunisolar)==
'''Lunisolar October''' (旧暦10月) is the tenth [[:en:Month|Month (calendar)]] of the {{ill|Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} ([[:en:Lunisolar calendar|Lunisolar calendar]]).
Before the adoption of the [[:en:Tenpō calendar|Tenpō calendar]], Lunisolar October was defined as the month containing [[:en:Xiaoxue|Shōsetsu (solar term)]]. In the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|New Calendar]], it corresponds roughly to late [[:en:October|October]] through early [[:en:December|December]].
Lunisolar October is also called {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|神無月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, although in {{ill|Izumo Province|ja|Izumo Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, particularly in [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], it is referred to as {{ill|Kamiarizuki|ja|神在月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiarizuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} or {{ill|Kamiaritsuki|ja|神有月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiaritsuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}}. For the etymology, see [[#Etymology]]{{efn|October|ja|10月|qq=draft}}.
In the East Asian lunisolar calendar, the number of days in each month ({{ill|Days in a lunar month|ja|大小|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Days in a lunar month|1=Large and Small|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10935019}}, 30-day "big months" and 29-day "small months") varies by year. As a result, some years have only 29 days in Lunisolar October, making {{ill|October 30 (Lunisolar)|ja|10月30日 (旧暦)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 30 (Lunisolar)|qq=}} nonexistent.
==Overview==
'''Kannazuki''' (神無月, also read as ''Kaminazuki''<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>), alternatively written as ''Kamnazuki''<ref name="ReferenceA">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.412, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>, ''Kaminashizuki,'' or ''Kaminakarizuki''<ref name="ReferenceB">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 978-4167598082</ref>, is an name for the {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|10月 (旧暦)|lt=10th month of the Japanese Lunar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. In modern times, it is also commonly used as an alternate name for October in the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]. The interpretation of "神無" ("absence of gods") is a {{ill|folk etymology|ja|語源俗解|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/folk etymology|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 民間語源|1=folk etymology|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109964}}, which later gave rise to various legends (discussed below).
== Etymology == {{See also|October|qq=}} The origin of the term "Kannazuki" is unclear. A prominent theory suggests that the "na" in "Kannazuki" is a possessive particle meaning "of," thus translating to "Month of the Gods." This interpretation is supported by the [[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]]. This is analogous to the term [[:en:Minazuki|Minazuki]] ("Month of Water"), where "na" also functions as a possessive particle (see {{ill|June#Etymology of Minazuki|ja|6月#水無月の語源|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June#Etymology of Minazuki|1=June|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q120}}).
The belief that all [[:en:Kami|kami (Shinto deities)]] gather at {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} for an annual meeting, leaving other regions devoid of deities, is a later interpretation from the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]. This folk etymology was spread nationwide by the {{ill|Onshi|ja|御師|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onshi|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} of [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]].<ref>Such folk explanations appear in texts like "Ōgishō" (旺文社古語辞典, 8th ed., p.332, 1994).</ref><ref>The attribution of "神無月" to the 10th month likely began in the Heian period. Theories on its meaning include "Month of Brewing" (醸成月) and "Month of Kannamesai" (神嘗月) (Suzuki Tōzō, 日常語語源辞典, p.80, Tōkyōdō, 1992).</ref><ref>Takashima Toshio noted, "Kannazuki has ancient folk etymologies, suggesting it means 'month without gods,' which arose from misunderstanding the original meaning of 'Kaminazuki'" (高島俊男, お言葉ですが, p.88, Bungeishunjū, 2006).</ref>
Even in [[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa Prefecture]], where Onshi activities were absent, the lunar October is called "飽果十月" (meaning "fruitless October") because no religious events are held during this time.<ref name='gyoji'>{{Cite book |editor=[[Nishikado Masayoshi]] |date=1958-05-23 |title=Encyclopedia of Annual Events |publisher=Tōkyōdō Shuppan |page=18|qq=}}</ref>
== Folk Traditions Based on "Kami Absent" == The idea that deities gather in {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} during October led to the belief that this region experiences a divine presence while the rest of Japan does not. Consequently, in Izumo, October is called '''Kamiarizuki''' (神在月 or 神有月, meaning "Month with Gods"), reflecting the opposite belief. This folk belief has been present since the [[:en:Middle Ages|medieval period]].<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.120, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976.</ref>
=== Kami Arrival and Departure Rituals === ==== In Izumo ==== In Izumo, several shrines, including [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], conduct rituals known as "Kamiarizuki" during the lunar October: * On the night of {{ill|10th day of the 10th lunar month|ja|10月10日 (旧暦)|1=October 10 (Lunisolar)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10th day of the 10th lunar month|13=User:Immanuelle/October 10 (Lunisolar)|qq=}}, the {{ill|Kami-mukae-sai|ja|神迎祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-mukae-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Welcoming of the Deities") is held at {{ill|Inasa Beach|ja|稲佐浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inasa Beach|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲佐の浜}}. This is followed by the {{ill|Kamiari-sai|ja|神在祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiari-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} at Izumo Taisha from the 11th to the 17th, with the {{ill|Karasade-sai|ja|神等去出祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karasade-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Farewell of the Deities") on the 18th.
==== In Nagano ==== At {{ill|Mount Iizuna|ja|飯綱山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Iizuna|1=Mount Iizuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666650}} in Nagano, rituals for "sending off" and "welcoming back" deities from Izumo were traditionally held. These events, involving torch-lighting, were discontinued after fires occurred in the Meiji period.<ref>{{Cite book |author=Nagano Prefecture Saku City Board of Education |date=1978-11-15 |title=Oral Legends of Kita-Saku |page=78|qq=}}</ref>

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[en:Kannazuki]][[it:Kannazuki]][[ja:神無月]][[ko:신무월]][[uk:Каннадзукі]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q6364021]] Wikidata name: Kannazuki [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:18, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:22, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:02, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Lunisolar October|qq=}} {{for|the Japanese comedian|Kannazuki (comedian)|qq=}} {{Italic title|qq=}} {{refimprove|date=November 2020|qq=}} {{nihongo|'''''Kannazuki'''''|神無月||also ''Kaminazuki'', ''Kaminashizuki''|qq=}} is a traditional name for the tenth month in the traditional [[Japanese calendar]]. Sometimes called Lunar [[:en:October|October]].
The name can be translated literally as "the month when there are no gods".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Izumo|title=Izumo {{!|qq=}} Japan|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> In [[Shinto]] tradition it was said that the eight million gods of Japan left their shrines and congregated annually at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]]. There the month was known as {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神在月|qq=}}, "the month when the gods are present".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kamiarizuki|title=Kamiarizuki {{!|qq=}} Shinto|website=Encyclopedia Britannica|language=en|access-date=2019-04-24|qq=}}</ref> However, the 無 character, which normally means "absent" or "there is not", is here probably originally used as an [[:en:Ateji|Ateji]], that is used only for the sound "na". In this name the "na" is actually a possessive particle, so ''Kaminazuki'' means "month of the gods", not "month without gods" ''(Kaminakizuki)'', similarly to ''Minazuki'', the "month of water". However, by false etymology this became commonly interpreted to mean that because in that month, all the Shinto ''[[kami]]'' gather at [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Shrine]] in Izumo province (modern-day [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]]), there are no gods in the rest of the country with the exception of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], who does not hear the summons and is thus still available for worship. Thus, in Izumo Province, the month is called {{nihongo|''Kamiarizuki''|神有月 or 神在月|"month with gods"|qq=}}.
Until 1873, the tenth month of the lunar calendar largely overlapped with the modern month of November. However, after the adoption of the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]] in Japan in that year, October became generally accepted as the "godless month".
==October (Lunisolar)==
'''Lunisolar October''' (旧暦10月) is the tenth [[:en:Month|Month (calendar)]] of the {{ill|Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} ([[:en:Lunisolar calendar|Lunisolar calendar]]).
Before the adoption of the [[:en:Tenpō calendar|Tenpō calendar]], Lunisolar October was defined as the month containing [[:en:Xiaoxue|Shōsetsu (solar term)]]. In the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|New Calendar]], it corresponds roughly to late [[:en:October|October]] through early [[:en:December|December]].
Lunisolar October is also called {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|神無月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, although in {{ill|Izumo Province|ja|Izumo Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, particularly in [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], it is referred to as {{ill|Kamiarizuki|ja|神在月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiarizuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} or {{ill|Kamiaritsuki|ja|神有月|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiaritsuki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}}. For the etymology, see [[#Etymology]]{{efn|October|ja|10月|qq=draft}}.
In the East Asian lunisolar calendar, the number of days in each month ({{ill|Days in a lunar month|ja|大小|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Days in a lunar month|1=Large and Small|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10935019}}, 30-day "big months" and 29-day "small months") varies by year. As a result, some years have only 29 days in Lunisolar October, making {{ill|October 30 (Lunisolar)|ja|10月30日 (旧暦)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 30 (Lunisolar)|qq=}} nonexistent.
==Overview==
'''Kannazuki''' (神無月, also read as ''Kaminazuki''<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>), alternatively written as ''Kamnazuki''<ref name="ReferenceA">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.412, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 4095220058</ref>, ''Kaminashizuki,'' or ''Kaminakarizuki''<ref name="ReferenceB">[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.136, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976, ISBN 978-4167598082</ref>, is an name for the {{ill|Kannazuki|ja|10月 (旧暦)|lt=10th month of the Japanese Lunar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannazuki|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. In modern times, it is also commonly used as an alternate name for October in the [[:en:Gregorian calendar|Gregorian calendar]]. The interpretation of "神無" ("absence of gods") is a {{ill|folk etymology|ja|語源俗解|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/folk etymology|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 民間語源|1=folk etymology|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109964}}, which later gave rise to various legends (discussed below).
== Etymology == {{See also|October|qq=}} The origin of the term "Kannazuki" is unclear. A prominent theory suggests that the "na" in "Kannazuki" is a possessive particle meaning "of," thus translating to "Month of the Gods." This interpretation is supported by the [[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]]. This is analogous to the term [[:en:Minazuki|Minazuki]] ("Month of Water"), where "na" also functions as a possessive particle (see {{ill|June#Etymology of Minazuki|ja|6月#水無月の語源|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June#Etymology of Minazuki|1=June|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q120}}).
The belief that all [[:en:Kami|kami (Shinto deities)]] gather at {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} for an annual meeting, leaving other regions devoid of deities, is a later interpretation from the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]. This folk etymology was spread nationwide by the {{ill|Onshi|ja|御師|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onshi|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} of [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]].<ref>Such folk explanations appear in texts like "Ōgishō" (旺文社古語辞典, 8th ed., p.332, 1994).</ref><ref>The attribution of "神無月" to the 10th month likely began in the Heian period. Theories on its meaning include "Month of Brewing" (醸成月) and "Month of Kannamesai" (神嘗月) (Suzuki Tōzō, 日常語語源辞典, p.80, Tōkyōdō, 1992).</ref><ref>Takashima Toshio noted, "Kannazuki has ancient folk etymologies, suggesting it means 'month without gods,' which arose from misunderstanding the original meaning of 'Kaminazuki'" (高島俊男, お言葉ですが, p.88, Bungeishunjū, 2006).</ref>
Even in [[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa Prefecture]], where Onshi activities were absent, the lunar October is called "飽果十月" (meaning "fruitless October") because no religious events are held during this time.<ref name='gyoji'>{{Cite book |editor=[[Nishikado Masayoshi]] |date=1958-05-23 |title=Encyclopedia of Annual Events |publisher=Tōkyōdō Shuppan |page=18|qq=}}</ref>
== Folk Traditions Based on "Kami Absent" == The idea that deities gather in {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} during October led to the belief that this region experiences a divine presence while the rest of Japan does not. Consequently, in Izumo, October is called '''Kamiarizuki''' (神在月 or 神有月, meaning "Month with Gods"), reflecting the opposite belief. This folk belief has been present since the [[:en:Middle Ages|medieval period]].<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.120, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976.</ref>
=== Kami Arrival and Departure Rituals === ==== In Izumo ==== In Izumo, several shrines, including [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], conduct rituals known as "Kamiarizuki" during the lunar October: * On the night of {{ill|10th day of the 10th lunar month|ja|10月10日 (旧暦)|1=October 10 (Lunisolar)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10th day of the 10th lunar month|13=User:Immanuelle/October 10 (Lunisolar)|qq=}}, the {{ill|Kami-mukae-sai|ja|神迎祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-mukae-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Welcoming of the Deities") is held at {{ill|Inasa Beach|ja|稲佐浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inasa Beach|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲佐の浜}}. This is followed by the {{ill|Kamiari-sai|ja|神在祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiari-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} at Izumo Taisha from the 11th to the 17th, with the {{ill|Karasade-sai|ja|神等去出祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karasade-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Farewell of the Deities") on the 18th.
==== In Nagano ==== At {{ill|Mount Iizuna|ja|飯綱山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Iizuna|1=Mount Iizuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666650}} in Nagano, rituals for "sending off" and "welcoming back" deities from Izumo were traditionally held. These events, involving torch-lighting, were discontinued after fires occurred in the Meiji period.<ref>{{Cite book |author=Nagano Prefecture Saku City Board of Education |date=1978-11-15 |title=Oral Legends of Kita-Saku |page=78|qq=}}</ref>

This is analogous to the term [[:en:Minazuki|Minazuki]] ("Month of Water"), where "na" also functions as a possessive particle (see {{ill|June#Etymology of Minazuki|ja|6月#水無月の語源|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/June#Etymology of Minazuki|1=June|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q120}}).
The belief that all [[:en:Kami|kami (Shinto deities)]] gather at {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} for an annual meeting, leaving other regions devoid of deities, is a later interpretation from the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]. This folk etymology was spread nationwide by the {{ill|Onshi|ja|御師|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onshi|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} of [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]].<ref>Such folk explanations appear in texts like "Ōgishō" (旺文社古語辞典, 8th ed., p.332, 1994).</ref><ref>The attribution of "神無月" to the 10th month likely began in the Heian period. Theories on its meaning include "Month of Brewing" (醸成月) and "Month of Kannamesai" (神嘗月) (Suzuki Tōzō, 日常語語源辞典, p.80, Tōkyōdō, 1992).</ref><ref>Takashima Toshio noted, "Kannazuki has ancient folk etymologies, suggesting it means 'month without gods,' which arose from misunderstanding the original meaning of 'Kaminazuki'" (高島俊男, お言葉ですが, p.88, Bungeishunjū, 2006).</ref>
Even in [[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa Prefecture]], where Onshi activities were absent, the lunar October is called "飽果十月" (meaning "fruitless October") because no religious events are held during this time.<ref name='gyoji'>{{Cite book |editor=[[Nishikado Masayoshi]] |date=1958-05-23 |title=Encyclopedia of Annual Events |publisher=Tōkyōdō Shuppan |page=18|qq=}}</ref>
== Folk Traditions Based on "Kami Absent" == The idea that deities gather in {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|1=Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395836}} during October led to the belief that this region experiences a divine presence while the rest of Japan does not. Consequently, in Izumo, October is called '''Kamiarizuki''' (神在月 or 神有月, meaning "Month with Gods"), reflecting the opposite belief. This folk belief has been present since the [[:en:Middle Ages|medieval period]].<ref>[[:en:Nihon Kokugo Daijiten|Nihon Kokugo Daijiten]], Vol. 5, p.120, Shogakukan, May 1, 1976.</ref>
=== Kami Arrival and Departure Rituals === ==== In Izumo ==== In Izumo, several shrines, including [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], conduct rituals known as "Kamiarizuki" during the lunar October: * On the night of {{ill|10th day of the 10th lunar month|ja|10月10日 (旧暦)|1=October 10 (Lunisolar)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10th day of the 10th lunar month|13=User:Immanuelle/October 10 (Lunisolar)|qq=}}, the {{ill|Kami-mukae-sai|ja|神迎祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-mukae-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Welcoming of the Deities") is held at {{ill|Inasa Beach|ja|稲佐浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inasa Beach|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲佐の浜}}. This is followed by the {{ill|Kamiari-sai|ja|神在祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiari-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神無月|1=Kannazuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6364021}} at Izumo Taisha from the 11th to the 17th, with the {{ill|Karasade-sai|ja|神等去出祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karasade-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ("Farewell of the Deities") on the 18th.
==== In Nagano ==== At {{ill|Mount Iizuna|ja|飯綱山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Iizuna|1=Mount Iizuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666650}} in Nagano, rituals for "sending off" and "welcoming back" deities from Izumo were traditionally held. These events, involving torch-lighting, were discontinued after fires occurred in the Meiji period.<ref>{{Cite book |author=Nagano Prefecture Saku City Board of Education |date=1978-11-15 |title=Oral Legends of Kita-Saku |page=78|qq=}}</ref>
